answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through credit networks where each agent is a vertex in a peer-vouched trust graph. To stem the tide of forged identities, transaction clearance enforces max-flow capacity limits signed with falcon cryptographic keys. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of locking real collateral per fabricated vertex, unable to widen the cut to honest nodes. However, this mechanism constrains capital liquidity and isolates newly initialized agents.
